rv.q: The play is only 90 minutes and, right now, it feels rather more like a very promising pilot to me.
THE TARGETED succeeds as both a dark comedy and a compassionate examination of human connection.
What's different about 'The Targeted' — and I found this refreshing — is that it's neither satire nor thriller.
It's a remarkably assured and empathetic piece that knows when to draw humor from the absurdity of the TI claims, and when to prod the deeper voids and losses.
Ms. West is the heartbeat of this production and one of the best reasons for seeing this play.
Kime's script is steeped in heart, humor and horror.
Kime builds a case for compassion with The Targeted .
It's a challenging and fascinating story that's written here, dealing in conspiracy, harassment and human obsession—only a few of society's ills touched in a well-conceived script.

The Targeted has a terrific premise and director Grace Dolezal-Ng makes the most of a wonderful cast. It is also quite gripping and very funny — especially when Grimm is on stage — but as the play went on, I felt a sense of a missed opportunity.
But the pace is sluggish and nothing much happens in The Targeted to appeal to an audience that might have been expecting a more rousing assault on a government about which many of us are suspicious.
Everything about this production feels carefully calibrated and emotionally precise.

cn.t: Kime's world premiere about conspiracy theorists and "targeted individuals" draws mostly positive reviews for its sensitive, darkly comic exploration of paranoia and community, though some critics find the premise more intriguing than the execution.
